summary:
Earth Sonic is an accessible web-based jukebox that transforms NASA Earth data and scientific visualizations into music, making our planet's changes easier to explore through sound.

Users can choose data records such as global temperature, atmospheric CO₂, sea level, or explore locations on an interactive 3D globe to hear changes in air temperature, rainfall, sunshine, and ocean temperature. They can also upload images, sequences, or videos into the Frame Lab and convert visual data into sound.

Earth Sonic addresses the Earth Information Jukebox challenge through Data Sonification. Scientific values are mapped to musical features such as pitch, rhythm, volume, brightness, and stereo position. Its interactive audio player includes adjustable speed and volume, spoken values, screen-reader support, keyboard navigation, audio legends, and downloadable WAV files.

Our project is designed especially for blind and low-vision users, allowing them to explore Earth information without relying on visual maps alone. By combining science, technology, music, and accessibility, Earth Sonic creates a new way to experience and understand our changing planet through sound.
details:
Earth Sonic is an interactive website that transforms NASA Earth data and scientific visualizations into music. Our goal is to make information about our planet accessible to everyone, especially people who are blind or have low vision.

We developed three main features: a Data Jukebox, an Interactive 3D Globe, and a Frame Lab. Users can listen to scientific records such as global temperature, carbon dioxide, and sea level changes. They can also select locations on the globe to explore temperature, rainfall, sunshine, and ocean temperature over time. In the Frame Lab, users can upload scientific images or videos and convert their visual information into sound.

The website works through Data Sonification: data values control musical features such as pitch, while changes over time create different rhythms. This allows listeners to explore scientific patterns through sound rather than relying only on visual charts and maps.

We used React, JavaScript, Vite, Web Audio API, Canvas, and Web Speech API to develop the website. We also included keyboard navigation, screen-reader support, spoken values, audio explanations, and downloadable WAV files.

Earth Sonic combines science, music, and technology to make Earth information more inclusive and engaging. We also focused on scientific accuracy, reliable data sources, accessibility, and ease of use.
